Alt text: In sum, no appellant has standing to appeal.
III. Conclusion
The court concludes that no appellant has standing to appeal the October 2025 order that
“[t]he automatic stay imposed under Section 362(a) of the Bankruptcy Code in the Jones
Bankruptcy Case does not apply to FSS or any of FSS’s asset.” (Docket Entry No. 2-30 at 2). The

motion to strike, (Docket Entry No. 38), is denied as moot.
The October 2025 order remains operative. Jones and/or Free Speech Systems may move
to stay the October 2025 order pending appeal to the Fifth Circuit by Friday, May 22, 2026.

 ________________________________
 Lee H. Rosenthal

Bankruptcy Case does not apply to FSS or any of FSS’s asset.” (Docket Entry No. 2-30 at 2). The
court lacks jurisdiction over this appeal. The appeal is dismissed.

sources.title: Alex Jones asks Houston judge to revive Infowars bankruptcy case
sources.snippet: # Alex Jones wants to return Infowars to federal bankruptcy, as The Onion pursues takeover. With Alex Jones’ Infowars website shut down and Texas state courts considering a plan to allow it to be taken over by The Onion, Jones this week asked a Houston federal judge to return the ownership fight to bankruptcy court. The conspiracy theorist’s lawyers appeared Friday in a Houston courtroom to argue that Senior U.S. District Judge Lee Rosenthal should reverse a bankruptcy judge’s decision last year that the bankruptcy court could not sell the Infowars assets. U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Christopher Lopez’s ruling moved the issue of Infowars ownership back to a Travis County court, where Jones lost a defamation case to families of Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting victims. Friday’s hearing, which Jones did not attend, was the latest in a jumble of legal tactics he's using to keep the issue of Infowars’ ownership alive in the courts.
sources.content: With Alex Jones’ Infowars website shut down and Texas state courts considering a plan to allow it to be taken over by The Onion, Jones this week asked a Houston federal judge to return the ownership fight to bankruptcy court. The conspiracy theorist’s lawyers appeared Friday in a Houston courtroom to argue that Senior U.S. District Judge Lee Rosenthal should reverse a bankruptcy judge’s decision last year that the bankruptcy court could not sell the Infowars assets. U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Christopher Lopez’s ruling moved the issue of Infowars ownership back to a Travis County court, where Jones lost a defamation case to families of Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting victims. The judge effectively ended the bankruptcy case in February. Advertisement Article continues below this ad Friday’s hearing, which Jones did not attend, was the latest in a jumble of legal tactics he's using to keep the issue of Infowars’ ownership alive in the courts. In 2022, Jones was ordered to pay more than $1.4 billion in damages to the families of Sandy Hook victims. He filed for personal bankruptcy after those civil judgments in Connecticut and Texas. Through the bankruptcy court, some of his assets, including real estate and a watch collection, have been sold. Infowars, the company he is famous for creating and promoting, has remained on the shelf. Advertisement Article continues below this ad Lopez had rejected an auction of Infowars assets, saying he was unsatisfied with the results. He later announced that a bankruptcy trustee could only sell Jones’ equity in Infowars. He said Sandy Hook families should try to satisfy their claims through state courts. Ben Broocks, Jones’ lawyer, said Friday that Lopez erred by declaring that the bankruptcy court could not sell the Infowars assets after he had previously authorized a plan to do so. Broocks said assets owned by Free Speech Systems, which is Infowars’ parent, should be sold at auction, an idea Lopez rejected last year. Lawyers representing the Sandy Hook families told Rosenthal the opposite. In their telling, Lopez realized he had made a mistake and then issued the correct ruling. “Initially, the bankruptcy court did try to authorize the trustee to sell it,” Kyle Kimpler said. “Later, the bankruptcy court realized it shouldn’t have done that.” Advertisement Article continues below this ad Kimpler also noted that the trustee for Jones' estate, who is legally in charge of his financial assets, did not support Jones' challenges to the ruling. Jones has no standing to argue about how the site is sold, Kimpler said. Any money derived from a sale would go to the families he owes money to. “Mr. Jones has no interest in the proceeding anymore,” Kimpler said. “There is no universe where the answer is Mr. Jones should administer these assets.” The appeal had been pending for months before The Onion announced its latest plan to take control of Infowars by leasing the platform from a state-appointed receiver. The Onion's representatives said in April they planned to pay $81,000 a month to rent the domain and turn it into a parody of the original site. The 3rdCourt of Appeals stayed the plan the day a judge was set to be briefed about it and possibly allow it to go forward. The same day, Infowars apparently shut down after a court-appointed receiver over the state case ordered Jones out of the company’s studio. Jones still has “absolute decision making power” over Infowars because he is still the manager of the LLC, Broocks said. InfoWars, the Austin, Texas based outlet operated by Free Speech Systems LLC, has ceased broadcasting and shuttered its physical studio following actions by a court appointed receiver. The developments stem from long-standing efforts by families of Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting victims to collect on multimillion and billion-dollar defamation judgments awarded against alex jones. This article provides a factual overview of the bankruptcy filings, key court rulings, and the most recent 2026 updates. sources.content: As of May 2026, the legal proceedings involving alex jones and his media platform InfoWars remain in active litigation across federal and state courts. InfoWars, the Austin, Texas based outlet operated by Free Speech Systems LLC, has ceased broadcasting and shuttered its physical studio following actions by a court appointed receiver. The developments stem from long-standing efforts by families of Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting victims to collect on multimillion and billion-dollar defamation judgments awarded against alex jones. This article provides a factual overview of the bankruptcy filings, key court rulings, and the most recent 2026 updates. It explains the legal processes involved in plain terms while referencing established court procedures and regulatory frameworks under U.S. bankruptcy law and state collection remedies. Background of the Defamation Judgments In 2022, civil juries in Connecticut and Texas found alex jones liable for defamation after he repeatedly claimed on InfoWars that the 2012 Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting was a hoax staged by crisis actors. The judgments totaled more than $1.4 billion, including compensatory and punitive damages awarded to the families of victims and an FBI agent who responded to the scene. These verdicts followed default judgments entered after alex jones failed to comply with discovery orders in the underlying lawsuits. The families alleged that alex jones’ statements led to years of harassment, stalking, and emotional distress. Courts in both states upheld the awards, and the U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear alex jones’ appeal of the Connecticut judgment in October 2025, leaving the rulings intact. Under standard civil procedure, plaintiffs (here, the Sandy Hook families) became judgment creditors entitled to collect through asset seizure, garnishment, or other post judgment remedies. When collection efforts encountered resistance, the cases moved into bankruptcy and state receivership proceedings. The Bankruptcy Filing and Federal Court Rulings Alex jones and Free Speech Systems LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas (Houston division) in late 2022. Chapter 11 typically allows a debtor to reorganize operations while proposing a plan to repay creditors over time. The filings triggered an automatic stay under the Bankruptcy Code, temporarily halting most collection actions by the Sandy Hook families. U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Christopher M. Lopez presided over the cases. In June 2024, Judge Lopez converted alex jones’ personal Chapter 11 case to a Chapter 7 liquidation, a process in which a trustee sells non exempt assets to distribute proceeds to creditors according to priority rules under the Bankruptcy Code. The judge simultaneously dismissed the Chapter 11 case of Free Speech Systems LLC after the parties could not agree on a reorganization plan. A bankruptcy auction of InfoWars assets occurred in late 2024. The Onion, a satirical news outlet, was initially declared the winning bidder. However, Judge Lopez rejected the sale in December 2024, citing flaws in the auction process and concerns that higher offers might have been possible. The ruling limited the bankruptcy trustee’s authority primarily to alex jones’ personal equity interest in the company rather than the full operational assets of Free Speech Systems. By early 2026, Judge Lopez’s decisions effectively ended the core federal bankruptcy proceedings for the company and shifted unresolved asset liquidation issues back to the state courts where the original defamation judgments were entered. This procedural step is common when bankruptcy courts determine that certain collection matters are better resolved under state law remedies. sources.title: Alex Jones asks Houston judge to halt Infowars handoff to The Onion
sources.snippet: # Alex Jones asks Houston judge to block hearing that could hand Infowars to The Onion. **Update:** On Wednesday night, the Texas 3rd Court of Appeals issued a stay of the turnover of Free Speech Systems' assets. As of Thursday morning, lawyers for the Sandy Hook families had asked the Texas Supreme Court to remove the stay. Infowars founder Alex Jones asked a federal judge in Houston to stop Thursday's hearing in Austin that could hand over control of the infamous website to The Onion. Jones called The Onion's plan to replace his Infowars with a satirical version of the site, including an impersonator who sounds like him, a "planned deception of millions of citizens" that warranted the court's immediate attention. The Onion last week announced plans to lease the Infowars domain and intellectual property from a court-appointed receiver who had been put in control of Free Speech Systems' assets by Travis County District Judge Maya Guerra Gamble.
sources.content: Infowars founder Alex Jones asked a federal judge in Houston to stop Thursday's hearing in Austin that could hand over control of the infamous website to The Onion. Advertisement Article continues below this ad Lawyers representing Jones filed a motion for expedited emergency injunctive relief in the Southern District of Texas on Tuesday. The motion asks District Judge Lee H. Rosenthal to stop a court-appointed receiver from selling or transferring rights to assets belonging to Free Speech Systems, the parent company of Infowars. In the filing, Jones said an injunction is needed "to prevent a gross miscarriage of justice." Jones called The Onion's plan to replace his Infowars with a satirical version of the site, including an impersonator who sounds like him, a "planned deception of millions of citizens" that warranted the court's immediate attention. Advertisement Article continues below this ad The Onion last week announced plans to lease the Infowars domain and intellectual property from a court-appointed receiver who had been put in control of Free Speech Systems' assets by Travis County District Judge Maya Guerra Gamble. The lease proposal was scheduled to be presented to Guerra Gamble on Thursday morning. Jones owes more than $1 billion to the families of Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting victims, who successfully sued him in Texas and Connecticut for defamation after he used his Infowars shows and website to imply the massacre was staged. Efforts to liquidate Jones' assets in federal bankruptcy proceedings failed in 2024, sending questions about how the families would be paid back for their judgments back to the state court. However, Jones had kept his case alive in the federal court system by arguing that the Infowars assets should be protected by bankruptcy law. Jones has separately asked the Texas 3rd Court of Appeals to block Thursday's hearing, according to the Austin American-Statesman. In that motion, Jones accused the receiver of trying to destroy the value of Infowars' assets. Advertisement Article continues below this ad The Onion plans to turn Infowars into a mockery of the original site, as well as a platform for up-and-coming comedians. The Onion has already begun selling products branded with its own version of Infowars' wordmark, replacing the O with the newspaper's vegetable logo. Money from the new Infowars is expected to go to the Sandy Hook victims.

In sum, no appellant has standing to appeal.
III. Conclusion
The court concludes that no appellant has standing to appeal the October 2025 order that
“[t]he automatic stay imposed under Section 362(a) of the Bankruptcy Code in the Jones
Bankruptcy Case does not apply to FSS or any of FSS’s asset.” (Docket Entry No. 2-30 at 2). The
court lacks jurisdiction over this appeal. The appeal is dismissed.
The motion for leave to file a corrected reply, (Docket Entry No. 37), is granted. The
motion to strike, (Docket Entry No. 38), is denied as moot.
The October 2025 order remains operative. Jones and/or Free Speech Systems may move
to stay the October 2025 order pending appeal to the Fifth Circuit by Friday, May 22, 2026.
SIGNED on May 15, 2026, at Houston, Texas.
 ________________________________
 Lee H. Rosenthal
 Senior United States District Judg

sources.title: Alex Jones asks Houston judge to halt Infowars handoff to The Onion
sources.snippet: # Alex Jones asks Houston judge to block hearing that could hand Infowars to The Onion. **Update:** On Wednesday night, the Texas 3rd Court of Appeals issued a stay of the turnover of Free Speech Systems' assets. As of Thursday morning, lawyers for the Sandy Hook families had asked the Texas Supreme Court to remove the stay. Infowars founder Alex Jones asked a federal judge in Houston to stop Thursday's hearing in Austin that could hand over control of the infamous website to The Onion. Jones called The Onion's plan to replace his Infowars with a satirical version of the site, including an impersonator who sounds like him, a "planned deception of millions of citizens" that warranted the court's immediate attention. The Onion last week announced plans to lease the Infowars domain and intellectual property from a court-appointed receiver who had been put in control of Free Speech Systems' assets by Travis County District Judge Maya Guerra Gamble.
sources.content: Infowars founder Alex Jones asked a federal judge in Houston to stop Thursday's hearing in Austin that could hand over control of the infamous website to The Onion. Advertisement Article continues below this ad Lawyers representing Jones filed a motion for expedited emergency injunctive relief in the Southern District of Texas on Tuesday. The motion asks District Judge Lee H. Rosenthal to stop a court-appointed receiver from selling or transferring rights to assets belonging to Free Speech Systems, the parent company of Infowars. In the filing, Jones said an injunction is needed "to prevent a gross miscarriage of justice." Jones called The Onion's plan to replace his Infowars with a satirical version of the site, including an impersonator who sounds like him, a "planned deception of millions of citizens" that warranted the court's immediate attention. Advertisement Article continues below this ad The Onion last week announced plans to lease the Infowars domain and intellectual property from a court-appointed receiver who had been put in control of Free Speech Systems' assets by Travis County District Judge Maya Guerra Gamble. The lease proposal was scheduled to be presented to Guerra Gamble on Thursday morning. Jones owes more than $1 billion to the families of Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting victims, who successfully sued him in Texas and Connecticut for defamation after he used his Infowars shows and website to imply the massacre was staged. Efforts to liquidate Jones' assets in federal bankruptcy proceedings failed in 2024, sending questions about how the families would be paid back for their judgments back to the state court. However, Jones had kept his case alive in the federal court system by arguing that the Infowars assets should be protected by bankruptcy law. Jones has separately asked the Texas 3rd Court of Appeals to block Thursday's hearing, according to the Austin American-Statesman. In that motion, Jones accused the receiver of trying to destroy the value of Infowars' assets. Advertisement Article continues below this ad The Onion plans to turn Infowars into a mockery of the original site, as well as a platform for up-and-coming comedians. The Onion has already begun selling products branded with its own version of Infowars' wordmark, replacing the O with the newspaper's vegetable logo. Money from the new Infowars is expected to go to the Sandy Hook victims.
